-algebra structure.
That the
T
-algebra structure induced by
{\rtimes}^{\prime}
coincides with
{\rtimes}
follows from the universal property of
\mathbf{Alg}(T^{\prime})
with respect to graded algebra morphisms.

Suppose we have a
(p_{1},\ldots,p_{n})
-graded
T
-algebra morphism
\chi\colon(x_{1},{\rtimes}_{1})\to(x_{2},{\rtimes}_{2})
. The
T^{\prime}
-algebra morphism induced directly by
\chi
, and the
T^{\prime}
-algebra morphism induced from the
(T\mathbin{;}u_{T^{\prime}})
-algebra morphism are both given by
(\chi\mathbin{;}u_{T^{\prime}})
by definition. Thus the universal property of
\mathbf{Alg}(T^{\prime})
with respect to graded algebra morphisms implies that the induced
T
-algebra morphism is
\chi
.

The other direction follows immediately from the universal property of
\mathbf{Alg}(T^{\prime})
(with respect both to algebras and graded algebra morphisms).
∎

Definition 6.3
.

A relative adjunction
\ell\mathrel{\dashv_{j}}r
inducing a relative monad
T
is
strictly
j
-relatively monadic
(alternatively
strictly monadic relative to
j
, or simply
strictly
j
-monadic
) if
T
admits an algebra object and
\ell\mathrel{\dashv_{j}}r
is isomorphic to
f_{T}\mathrel{\dashv_{j}}u_{T}
in the category of resolutions of
T
.

Note that a tight-cell
r
is strictly
j
-monadic if and only if it admits a left
j
-adjoint and the induced
j
-adjunction is strictly
j
-monadic, since both properties exhibit
r
as being the right
j
-adjoint of a terminal resolution.

It follows from
Lemma

6.2
that the pasting law for relative adjunctions (
Lemma

6.1
) respects relative monadicity.

Lemma 6.4
.

Consider the following diagram.

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces C}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces D}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces A}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces E}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces r}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces j}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces r^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\ell^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\ell}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\dashv}

Suppose that
\ell^{\prime}\mathrel{\dashv_{j}}r^{\prime}
is strictly
j
-monadic. Then the left triangle exhibits a strictly
\ell^{\prime}
-monadic relative adjunction if and only if the outer triangle exhibits a strictly
j
-monadic relative adjunction.

Proof.

Follows directly from
Lemmas

6.1
and
6.2
, the latter exhibiting the universal properties of
\mathbf{Alg}(T)
and
\mathbf{Alg}(T\mathbin{;}r^{\prime})
as being equivalent.
∎

We rephrase
Lemma

6.4
to concern only the tight-cells
r
and
r^{\prime}
, rather than relative adjunctions, which gives necessary and sufficient conditions for the composite
(r\mathbin{;}r^{\prime})
to be relatively monadic.

Theorem 6.5

(Relative monadicity of composites)
.

Let
j\colon A\to E
and
r^{\prime}\colon D\to E
be tight-cells, and assume that
r^{\prime}
is (non)strictly
j
-monadic, with left
j
-adjoint
\ell^{\prime}
.
A tight-cell
r\colon C\to D
is (non)strictly
\ell^{\prime}
-monadic if and only if
(r\mathbin{;}r^{\prime})\colon C\to E
is (non)strictly
j
-monadic.

Proof.

Let
T^{\prime}
be the
j
-monad induced by
\ell^{\prime}\mathrel{\dashv_{j}}r^{\prime}
.
Without loss of generality, we may assume
\ell^{\prime}\mathrel{\dashv_{j}}r^{\prime}
is strictly
j
-monadic: the following diagram commutes, so that non-strict
\ell^{\prime}
-monadicity of
r
is equivalently non-strict
f_{T^{\prime}}
-monadicity of
(r\mathbin{;}{\simeq})
, and non-strict
j
-monadicity of
(r\mathbin{;}r^{\prime})
is equivalently non-strict
j
-monadicity of
(r\mathbin{;}{\simeq}\mathbin{;}u_{T^{\prime}})
.

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces D}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathbf{Alg}(T^{\prime})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces A}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces E}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces j}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces u_{T^{\prime}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{T^{\prime}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces r^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\ell^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\dashv}

The strict case then follows directly from
Lemma

6.4
, considering the following triangle, where
\ell\colon A\to C
is the left relative adjoint of either
r
or of
(r\mathbin{;}u_{T^{\prime}})
.

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces C}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathbf{Alg}(T^{\prime})}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces A}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces E}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces r}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces j}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces u_{T^{\prime}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{T^{\prime}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\ell}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\dashv}

The non-strict case follows therefrom by precomposing
r
by equivalences.
∎

Theorem

6.5
may be seen as a significant generalisation of classical sufficiency results for the monadicity of a composite
(r\mathbin{;}r^{\prime})
functor (e.g.
[
BW85
, Proposition 3.5.1]
). When
r
is fully faithful, it may alternatively be seen as a weakening of
[
Bir35
]
’s
HSP theorem

[
Bir35
, Theorem 10]
, giving necessary and sufficient conditions for a subcategory of a category of algebras to itself be a category of algebras (the HSP theorem further asks that, in this case, the induced monad morphism be a regular epimorphism, which expresses that the subcategory is formed by imposing additional axioms on the algebras).
4
4

4

While we expect that the HSP theorem may be derived from
Theorem

6.5
, we shall not do so here.

To conclude, we mention two useful consequences of
Theorem

6.5
. The first is the following classical cancellability result for monadic adjunctions (cf.
[
Bou92
, Proposition 5]
).

Corollary 6.6

(Cancellability)
.

Consider the following situation, in which the monad induced by
\ell\dashv r
admits an algebra object.

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces C}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces D}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces E}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces r}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces r^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\ell^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\ell}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\dashv}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\dashv}

If
r^{\prime}
and
(r\mathbin{;}r^{\prime})
are (non)strictly monadic, then so is
r
.

Proof.

From
Theorem

6.5
, we have that
r^{\prime}
is (non)strictly
\ell^{\prime}
-monadic. The result then follows from
Proposition

4.12
(
′
), since the monad induced by
\ell\dashv r
admits an algebra object.
∎

The second establishes that algebraic tight-cells – that is, those tight-cells between algebra objects that are induced by relative monad morphisms – create limits and certain colimits, and are themselves monadic as soon as they admit left adjoints.

Corollary 6.7
.

Let
j\colon A\to E
be a tight-cell, and consider a commutative triangle as follows, where
r
and
r^{\prime}
are (non)strictly
j
-monadic.

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{D^{\prime}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces D}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces E}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces r^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces r}

Then:

(6.7.(1))

i
(non)strictly creates limits and those colimits in
D
that are sent by
r
to
j
-absolute colimits.

(6.7.(2))

i
is (non)strictly monadic if and only if it admits a left adjoint.

Proof.

Denote by
\ell
the left
j
-adjoint of
r
.
By
Theorem

6.5
,
i
is (non)strictly
\ell
-monadic.

i
(non)strictly creates limits and
\ell
-absolute colimits by
Propositions

3.4
,
3.6
and
3.12
. In particular, the (non)strict lifting of any
j
-absolute colimit through
r
is

,

and

together with simple observations about the creation of limits and colimits, but find the approach above to be particularly satisfying.)

(2) follows immediately from

(
′

∎

The preservation of limits and certain colimits in
Corollary

6.7
is often sufficient, via an adjointness theorem, to imply that, for sufficiently nice roots
j
, every algebraic tight-cell admits a right adjoint, and hence is monadic.
We end with an example of this situation.

Example 6.8
.

From
Example

5.6
, we have that the category of algebras
\mathbf{Cart}[L{}^{\mathrm{op}},{\mathbf{Set}}]
of a finitary algebraic theory
\ell\colon{\mathbb{F}}\to L
is
(j\colon{\mathbb{F}}\hookrightarrow{\mathbf{Set}})
-monadic. Since
u_{\ell}
and
n_{j}
preserve sifted colimits, sifted colimits in
\mathbf{Cart}[L{}^{\mathrm{op}},{\mathbf{Set}}]
are lifted non-strictly by
u_{\ell}
via
Lemmas

5.1
and
3.12
. Consequently, every concrete functor
i
between categories of algebras for finitary algebraic theories preserves limits and sifted colimits.

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathbf{Cart}[L^{\prime}{}^{\mathrm{op}},{\mathbf{Set}}]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathbf{Cart}[L{}^{\mathrm{op}},{\mathbf{Set}}]}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathbf{Set}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces u_{\ell^{\prime}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces u_{\ell}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\dashv}

Since categories of algebras for algebraic theories are locally strongly finitely presentable, and every continuous and sifted-cocontinuous functor therebetween is a right adjoint, every such
i
is a right adjoint, and hence is non-strictly monadic (cf.
[
Law63
,
Man67
]
).
